scope: Independent review of PCM registration/unregistration source, original body evidence, direct-caller literals, observer audit, and representative native comparisons.

cases: queued notifications survive owner/callback replacement and removal
no-memory-hook versus scoped memory-hook stores/snapshot sequence

logger_flag_reread.mutation: Synthetic 0-to-1 FLAGS mutation between successive volatile reads; both sides stop at 0x43ce9e.

assessment.source: No blocking defect found in the bounded functions. FLAGS is separately volatile-read at each test; the compiled O2 code and synthetic reread test confirm this behavior.
assessment.atomicity: The memset byte/word store order is reconstructed; scalar C stores are not claimed atomic-equivalent to the grouped stock store.
assessment.observer_audit: No memory hooks during registration; final mapped RAM except stack/output, full I2S/SCB and normalized ordered store bytes compared. The 10-call no-hook/scoped-hook sequence matched. This is not a universal read-trace or physical-device proof.
limits: Callbacks, DSP, file sink, task wake/routing and PCM ownership are static or boundary-only.
No multiword atomicity, concurrent registration safety, physical cache/MMIO behavior, full source completeness, or byte-identical firmware claim.
